edbDesc: A wave travelling along the interface between two fluids, whose dynamics are dominated by the effects of surface tension. Capillary waves are common in nature and home, and are often referred to as ripple. The wavelength of capillary waves is typically less than a few centimeters. A gravity-capillary wave on a fluid interface is influenced by both the effects of surface tension and gravity, as well as by the fluid inertia.
title: Capillary Wave Effect
pickWhy: A type of ripple ruled by surface tension rather than an effect that does a job; its useful side (ultrasonic misting) belongs with Faraday waves in another batch.
